subject: Renewal + Premium SLO conversion & capacity uplift for LogiScale
messages:
From: Alice Romero <alice@logiscale.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@logiscale.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — premium SLO + throughput uplift

Sofia,

Hope you had a good week. Our renewal for LogiScale is coming up in September and we want to explore two changes before we sign:

- Move to a premium SLO (99.95% latency p95 target for endpoint /logi-query).
- Increase committed throughput by ~2.5x for peak batch windows (Q4 product launches).

I've attached a short usage export for Q2 that shows the burst patterns. We like Redwood's reliability but need assurance on latency tails and a predictable capacity plan if we commit to a larger spend.

Can we set a call next week to walk through options (canary rollout windows, staged capacity reservation, and any incremental ops support)? Also please outline any pricing implications for the premium SLO + dedicated uplift.

Thanks,
Alice Romero
Head of Procurement, LogiScale
Attachment: LogiScale_usage_Q2_2028.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Romero <alice@logiscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLO + throughput uplift

Alice — thanks for sending this over and for the clarity on requirements. Happy to run a short proposal and schedule a 30-minute sync with engineering + ops next Tuesday.

Quick notes up front so we can make the call productive:
- Premium SLO: we can support a 99.95% p95 latency target for the specified endpoint with a combination of dedicated lanes + prefetched KV caching. We typically validate with a 2-week canary on mirrored traffic.
- Throughput uplift: we recommend a staged reserve (50% commit now, additional reserve purchasable in month 2) to balance cost predictability and capacity availability for Q4 spikes.
- Pricing: premium SLO is structured as a fixed monthly retainer + per-token uplift on committed capacity. I'll include numbers in the proposal PDF.

Proposed meeting times (PDT): Tue Jul 23 10:00 or 14:00. Which works for your team?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@logiscale.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Romero <alice@logiscale.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLO + throughput uplift

Sofia / Ben —

Thanks for the quick reply. Jul 23 10:00 PDT works. A couple of clarifying items for the agenda so we can surface them to procurement and engineering:

1) Failure/rollback policy — if the canary shows regressions vs. current baseline, what's the auto-fallback plan and how long before we can revert?
2) Maintenance windows & scheduled migrations — our product team requires <=1 hour planned maintenance during business hours for control plane upgrades.
3) Credits & SLA remedies — if we miss the premium SLO, what's the crediting mechanism and how quickly are incidents adjudicated?

Also, Alice wanted me to flag that LogiScale's security team will ask about audit logs retention (we currently have a 13-month compliance requirement). Happy to share the contact during the call.

Jake Turner
Platform Reliability Lead, LogiScale
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Romero <alice@logiscale.com>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@logiscale.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-21T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLO + throughput uplift

Alice/Jake — appreciate the agenda items. Confirming the plan for our call Tue Jul 23 10:00 PDT (calendar invite sent). Drafting answers here so procurement has visibility before the meeting: 

- Canary rollback: the canary runs mirrored traffic to a dedicated pool. If we detect >=1.5x increase in p95 vs baseline for three contiguous 5-minute windows, the routing policy triggers automatic rollback to the previous model variant and route (we've done this previously for two enterprise customers). Rollback completes within the next token batch window (typically <90s). We will run a post-mortem within 48 hours and offer a one-time operational remediation runbook.

- Maintenance windows: we support configurable maintenance windows. For business-hours constraints we can apply a controlled-window SLA that limits noncritical migrations to off-peak, and critical patches will be coordinated with 72h notice and a guaranteed <=1 hour planned downtime for control-plane operations. Any emergency hotfixes will be communicated via the incident channel.

- Credits & remedies: premium SLO credits are tiered. For p95 breaches we offer a percentage credit against the monthly retainer depending on severity and duration; incidents are triaged in our ops dashboard and a remediation letter is issued within 7 business days. We can surface exact credit percentages in the SLA Addendum we send on Tuesday.

- Audit logs & retention: we can retain audit logs for 13 months in an encrypted bucket (KMS-managed). Option to extend retention is available as an add-on.

Attached is a draft SLA addendum with the above commitments and a pricing outline for the 2.5x uplift and staged reserve (Draft_SLA_Addendum_v3.pdf). If that looks good we can generate a DocuSign and set an implementation timeline (canary start + two-week validation + staged capacity activation).

Next steps for the meeting: 1) review SLA addendum and pricing, 2) confirm canary plan and rollback thresholds with your engineering lead, 3) identify security contact for audit logs.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Draft_SLA_Addendum_v3.pdf (PDF, 96KB)
